evidence: Single package (pyexcel_xlsx) with clear module separation (book.py, xlsxr.py, xlsxw.py) indicating internal modularity
Clean separation of concerns: Book/Sheet for core data model, xlsxr.py for reading, xlsxw.py for writing
Use of interfaces (ISheet, IReader, IWriter) from pyexcel_io plugin API suggests modular design with well-defined contracts
Test suite organized by functionality (test_book.py, test_reader.py, test_writer.py, etc.) with base classes for shared behavior
No evidence of network boundaries, services, or processes — all code in one repository/package
Average fan-out of ~3.6 suggests moderate coupling between modules, typical of monolithic designs
Directory depth of 3 reflects logical grouping without excessive nesting, common in well-structured monoliths
risks: Single point of failure if core modules become tightly coupled over time
Testing complexity may grow as test base expands (shared fixtures, inheritance hierarchies)
Limited scalability options without refactoring to decouple components
